items.label: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Photomask business plan (Nakanishi, head of Fine Device Operations)

set.signal: Photomask business plan (Nakanishi, head of Fine Device Operations): DNP aims for average annual photomask sales growth of more than 15% through FY2030 (the fiscal year ending March 2031), driven by commercialising cutting-edge technologies. After JPY20 billion of capex in April 2023 - March 2026 it is raising its photomask capex plan for April 2026 - March 2029 to JPY70 billion, covering EUV masks, nanoimprint and production capability from advanced areas to the volume zone, and expects sales in cutting-edge areas alone to rise by JPY24 billion in the year ending March 2029 versus the year ended March 2025. Management (Q&A): it cannot break down the JPY70 billion, but as EUV equipment is extremely expensive 'it is reasonable to assume' EUV accounts for a substantial proportion; capex for nanoimprint mass production is not yet included and will be decided once customers indicate production timing and volumes; the large photomask sales increase projected in its materials for the years ending March 2028 and March 2029 reflects capacity expansion through large-scale capex; growth is now forecast above last year's plan because EUV-related business has become more tangible and merchant sales volume is expected to be greater than anticipated last year, from higher order volumes at existing customers.

items.reason: Hedge dropped: management said it is 'reasonable to assume' EUV is a substantial part of the JPY70 billion, not that it is; restore the hedge (rest of the entry verified verbatim).
items.evidence: We cannot provide a detailed breakdown of the 70 billion yen. However, as is widely known, EUV equipment is extremely expensive, so it is reasonable to assume that investment in EUV accounts for a substantial proportion.

items.label: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Group plan detail (Senior Managing Director Miyake; management Q&A)

set.signal: Group plan detail (Senior Managing Director Miyake; management Q&A): operating profit is to grow about 9% a year from JPY101 billion (year ended March 2026) to JPY130 billion (year ending March 2029). Half of sales in the year to March 2026 came from the six focus businesses, which are to reach 57% by the year to March 2029, while businesses for reforming, cut from 48% of sales (year to March 2023) to 17% (year to March 2026), are to fall to 9%; the six focus businesses' total sales are to grow about 10% a year, from JPY510 billion (year to March 2023) and JPY606 billion (year to March 2026) to JPY808 billion (year to March 2029), with information security going from JPY187 billion to JPY271 billion (13% CAGR). More than 60% of the JPY200 billion growth capex goes to Electronics, especially semiconductors; because EUV, nanoimprint and glass cores are set to enter the mass-production phase during April 2026 - March 2029, DNP plans continued capex and possibly further capacity investment. Q&A: capex is not fixed at JPY200 billion and, through flexible allocation, semiconductor growth investment could exceed JPY120 billion. Structural reforms are to add JPY5 billion or more in the year ending March 2027.

items.reason: Period ambiguity: '17%' had no period ('fall from 48% (year to March 2023) and 17% to 9%'); the 17% is DNP's FY2025 (year to March 2026) and the 9% the plan's end (year to March 2029).
items.evidence: the business for reforming has been scaled back from 48% in FY2022 to 17%. During this medium-term management plan covering the years 2026 to 2028 ... our businesses for reforming account for 9%

items.label: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Digital Interface (Miyake): its main products are metal masks

set.signal: Digital Interface (Miyake): its main products are metal masks, increasingly for OLED, and optical films. Because of the semiconductor memory shortage some manufacturers find it difficult to produce smartphones in the short term, so DNP's metal-mask order volume is declining; smartphone OLED panel shipments are projected to decline in FY2026 (as DNP labels it; DNP's FY2026 runs April 2026 - March 2027) because of the memory shortage and to grow thereafter, for an average annual growth rate of 3%. Foldables could raise the OLED area per phone about three times, lifting metal-mask shipments; notebook PCs and tablets are forecast to grow about 29% a year and TV screens of 65 inches and larger about 6% a year in area. DNP will use its G8-size production line across more OLED panel types and raise utilisation of the line installed last September mainly for surface materials for 65-inch and larger panels; the goal is about 5% average annual sales growth.

items.reason: Fiscal-year trap: 'what DNP labels FY2026' left the period undefined (DNP's FY2026 = Apr 2026 - Mar 2027, the graph's FY2027); and the 3% is the forecast's average annual growth rate over the period, not growth 'thereafter'.
items.evidence: While shipments are projected to decline in FY2026 due to a shortage of semiconductor memory, they are expected to grow thereafter, resulting in an average annual growth rate of 3%.

set.signal: Smart Communication businesses: information security (Numano, Information Innovation Operations) - after consolidating Rubicon SEZC (government ID, focused on Africa) in July 2025, DNP announced a tender offer for AUSTRIACARD HOLDINGS AG on May 13, 2026 (customer base in Eastern Europe, the Middle East, Africa and North America in financial and government ID) to combine DNP's Asian, Rubicon's African and AUSTRIACARD's platforms with a focus on government IDs and ID authentication; the domestic digital ID and authentication market is expected to grow at a 7.8% CAGR; sales are planned to grow from 100 in FY2024 (year ended March 2025) to 167 by FY2030 (year ending March 2031), about 8.9% a year. Photo imaging (Murakami, Imaging Communications Operations) - more than 400,000 DNP printers operate in over 100 countries, producing about 5 billion photo prints a year, with manufacturing in Japan, the US, Malaysia and the Netherlands; an India subsidiary began sales in March 2026; sales are to grow from 100 in FY2024 to 129 by 2030 (4.4% a year) and profit to 175 (9.9% a year) through higher-value-added printers and media such as the DS820DX launched in 2024; 4-inch prints are about 80% of volume.

items.label: Dai Nippon Printing results briefing: FY2025 (ending March 31, 2026) Financial Results and New Medium-Term Management Plan (05-15-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Middle East situation (management, Q&A): Life & Healthcare

set.signal: Middle East situation (management, Q&A): Life & Healthcare is the most affected segment, mainly packaging, which uses many petroleum-based materials. Higher material prices are passed on with a time lag after they are confirmed, causing a JPY2 billion negative impact across all segments in the first quarter (April-June 2026) of the fiscal year ending March 2027, with pass-through assumed from the second quarter onward. Packaging customers accept increases relatively easily because they want uninterrupted supply, whereas Electronics prices usually decline daily but have recently fluctuated with the supply-demand balance, so passing on increases there may take time; management is concerned customers could cut purchases if increases become excessive, or suspend production because of material shortages or fuel costs.

items.reason: Period ambiguity: a bare 'Q1' under a label for the year ending March 2026 reads as April-June 2025; management meant Q1 of the forecast year (DNP's FY2026, ending March 2027), as the President's remarks and the Q1 deck state.
items.evidence: at this time we have incorporated only the negative impact of JPY2 billion on operating profit expected in Q1 into our earnings forecast. Taking into account the impact of the situation in the Middle East in this Q1, we project operating profit of JPY108 billion for FY2026.
